items.headline: Study says IRS cut conservation easement values by 97% on average
items.caption: A review of 130+ IRS valuation reviews found cuts of 99% or more were common. The IRS pointed to its new conservation easement office.

visual.title: Cleveland easement, two IRS reviews
visual.foot: Infinity Advisory study: avg cut ~97% across 115 cases

detail: A study by Infinity Advisory Services looked at more than 130 IRS valuation reviews. In 115 conservation easement cases, the IRS cut appraised values by about 97% on average.

In one Cleveland case, an IRS reviewer first valued a building's easement at $18.1 million to $23.2 million, then lowered it to $400,000. A whistleblower also raised concerns. These are allegations; the IRS cited its August statement.
In August, the IRS ended standard settlement offers and created an Office of Conservation Easements. Courts this year upheld big IRS cuts and 40% penalties in two Georgia cases.
money: Conservation easements can give real deductions, but big claims draw intense IRS review.
If someone pitches a deduction worth many times your investment, get an independent tax pro first.
Keep strong appraisals and records for any large donation deduction.

A plan's rating can change after lawsuits, so look at costs and your doctors too.

items: No new Medicare hospice or home health agencies
Some majority ownership changes also blocked
Enrolled agencies may now add locations
Current patients' care is not affected

detail: CMS said it will keep its nationwide moratorium on new Medicare hospice and home health agencies for six more months. The first freeze began May 13. Federal Register notices were set for November 16.
New agencies still can't enroll, and certain majority ownership changes are blocked. One change: agencies already enrolled can now add practice locations under their current enrollment.
CMS chief Mehmet Oz said fraud in these areas persists. In October, a two-day sweep in California led to 145 provider revocations tied to more than $703 million in Medicare and Medicaid payments.
money: Choosing an agency for a parent? Confirm it is already Medicare-enrolled and in your plan's network.
Check your Medicare statements for services you never got; report fraud to 1-800-MEDICARE.
Investors in home health companies may see less new competition.
risk: Fewer new agencies could mean longer waits in some areas.
Rules may change again when the freeze ends.

items.headline: Connecticut extends $300 grocery cards for ex-SNAP families to Dec. 31; few claimed
items.caption: Connecticut gave people who lost SNAP more time to pick up a $300 grocery gift card. Only about 2,000 of 25,000 eligible residents had one by late October.

visual.title: Connecticut's $300 grocery cards
visual.label: Share of eligible ex-SNAP residents who got a card by Oct. 27.

detail: Connecticut's Department of Social Services confirmed Monday it pushed the deadline for its $300 grocery gift cards from November 30 to December 31. The cards go to about 25,000 people who lost federal SNAP food aid.
Gov. Ned Lamont launched the $7.5 million program in June using state surplus money. As of October 27, only about 2,000 people had received a card.
Eligible residents can show ID at a local community action agency and get a card on the spot. The state plans another round of text messages.
money: If you lost SNAP in Connecticut, claim your $300 card at a community action agency before Dec. 31.
Know someone who lost SNAP? Share this; most eligible people haven't claimed it.
Check if your state has similar one-time food help; programs vary.
risk: Unclaimed cards after Dec. 31 may be lost.
Watch for scam texts; verify through the state or agency.

items.headline: Homan says ICE aims to top last year's record 483,200 deportations in 2027
items.caption: Border czar Tom Homan said ICE plans to break its deportation record again in fiscal 2027. He said the agency still has a couple thousand agents to hire.
detail: In a Fox News interview Monday, border czar Tom Homan said ICE plans to set a new deportation record in fiscal 2027. DHS has reported 483,200 deportations in fiscal 2026.
Homan said ICE still has a couple thousand agents to hire. He said the agency faces more than 100 nationwide court orders and close to 100,000 habeas cases seeking release of detainees.
The comments came after Republican losses in the midterms. Critics point to court data showing many rulings against the administration's enforcement moves.
money: Industries that rely on immigrant labor, like farming and construction, may face worker shortages and higher costs.
Employers should keep I-9 and work authorization records current.
Families affected should know legal aid options; many groups offer free help.
risk: Court rulings could slow or change enforcement plans.
Hiring goals may not be met.

items.headline: Barclays starts cutting about 200 more investment bank jobs, on top of 5,000
items.caption: Barclays is cutting about 200 more investment banking roles, mostly in New York and London. It's part of an AI-backed cost plan that already targets about 5,000 jobs.

visual.title: Barclays cost cuts
visual.label: Extra investment bank jobs being cut, starting Tuesday.

detail: Barclays plans about 200 more layoffs in its investment bank, according to Bloomberg sources. The round begins Tuesday and hits staff at several levels, mostly in New York and London.
The cuts add to roughly 5,000 job reductions the bank announced with third-quarter results on October 22. Barclays is leaning on technology such as AI to cut costs.
Finance chief Anna Gross said the bank saved close to £700 million a year over the last two years and expects more than £1.1 billion in gross savings in 2027.
money: Finance workers: refresh your resume and network now; banks are trimming roles as AI spreads.
Bank cost cuts can lift profits and dividends for shareholders.
If laid off, check severance terms and roll your 401(k) carefully.
risk: More cuts could follow in 2027.
Cost cuts don't guarantee higher earnings.

items.headline: XPeng's sales jump 19% to a record, but its loss more than doubles
items.caption: Chinese EV maker XPeng delivered a record 118,390 cars last quarter. Revenue rose 19% while the net loss grew to about $130M and margins slipped.

visual.title: XPeng Q3 2026
visual.foot: Per XPeng's SEC filing

detail: XPeng said Tuesday it delivered 118,390 vehicles in the third quarter, up 2.1% from a year earlier and a company record. Revenue rose 19.1% to about RMB24.3 billion, or $3.62 billion.
Profitability went the wrong way. Gross margin fell to 18.9% from 20.1%, and the net loss widened to RMB0.87 billion from RMB0.38 billion.
For the fourth quarter, XPeng expects 169,000 to 174,000 deliveries and revenue up about 37% to 43%. It targets more than 100,000 overseas sales this year.
money: Growth stocks can rise on sales but fall on losses; read both lines before you buy.
EV price wars help car buyers; compare deals before purchasing.
Want China exposure? A broad fund spreads risk better than one stock.
risk: Price wars in China keep squeezing margins.
Trade rules can limit overseas sales.

items.headline: Moody's cuts Hertz deeper into junk at Caa1 as 2028 debt walls loom
items.caption: Moody's dropped Hertz two notches, from B2 to Caa1, with a negative outlook. About $3.7B of credit lines and loans come due in 2028.

visual.title: Hertz by the numbers
visual.foot: Per Moody's via Investing.com

detail: Moody's cut Hertz Global's corporate family rating to Caa1 from B2 on Monday and kept the outlook negative. It also lowered the company's liquidity score and the ratings on most of its debt.

The worry is refinancing. About $1.7 billion of revolving credit expires in March 2028 and nearly $2 billion of term loans come due that June. Moody's expects Hertz to lose money before taxes through 2027, with debt near 6.5 times earnings.
Hertz had $531 million in cash and $415 million of unused credit at the end of September. Another $200 million of unsecured notes matures next month.
money: Renting a car? Big rental firms under pressure may push prices or fees; compare Hertz, rivals and car-share apps before you book.
If you own Hertz bonds or a high-yield fund, check how much is in Caa-rated debt, which has a higher default risk.
A falling credit rating can mean cheap used rental cars hit the market; watch dealer prices if you shop for a used car.
risk: Moody's says more cuts could follow if refinancing stalls or used-car prices drop sharply.
Hertz stock was down about 6.7% when the downgrade report came out.

sources.t: Moody's downgrades Hertz to Caa1 as 2028 refinancing risks mount
